description.from:
**Follow-on under `PPY-54055d`.** Diagnose already fuses heuristics, profile `rules:`, and 4-gram redundancy. This slice adds **conventional density signals only**.

## Intent

As a publication operator, I want diagnose to flag long, low-content drafts using measures other people already use for how much is said per word — not sentence embeddings.

## Golden path (this story)

1. **Lexical density** (Ure/Halliday): content words / total words, via a closed-class function-word list (stdlib, no spaCy).
2. **gzip ratio**: compressed length / raw length.
3. **Existing 4-gram redundancy** (already in diagnose). Unchanged.

Independent findings plus a `density` summary. No weighted fluff score. Not an AI-detector.

## Out of scope (explicit)

- Sentence embeddings, fastembed, MiniLM, ONNX, TF-IDF sentence clustering, `concept_restatement`
- Homemade “concept count”
- Propositional idea density / CPIDR (later if we want it)
- Rewrite options (PPY-73906c), verifier (PPY-5ca22f), Newsroom UI

**Honest limit:** the same claim said three ways in different words will usually not fire these. Verbatim repeats stay on 4-grams.

## Done when

- `checks.informationDensity` (default on) and optional `density:` thresholds: `minWords`, `minLexicalDensity` (flag when below), `maxGzipRatio` (flag when gzip/raw is below this).
- Diagnose JSON includes `density`: `wordCount`, `sentenceCount`, `lexicalDensity`, `gzipRatio`. No `embedder` field.
- Long synthetic fluff produces `low_information_density` when `wordCount >= minWords`.
- A must-pass Anth.us reference excerpt above `minWords` does not.
- Short drafts below `minWords` do not get the document-level flag.

## Gherkin

```gherkin
Feature: Diagnose information density from conventional signals
  As a publication operator
  I want lexical density and compression in diagnose JSON
  So long padded drafts are a steer-able red flag

  Scenario: Density summary is present
    Given a loadable style profile with information density enabled
    And a draft of several sentences
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then the JSON includes density with wordCount, sentenceCount, lexicalDensity, and gzipRatio
    And the JSON does not include an embedder field

  Scenario: Long low-content fluff is flagged
    Given a draft longer than the profile minWords that is padded with function words and repeats
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there is a low_information_density finding

  Scenario: House-voice excerpt is not flagged as fluff
    Given a must-pass excerpt from an Anth.us reference sample longer than minWords
    And the Anth.us style profile
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there is no low_information_density finding

  Scenario: Short drafts skip the document-level density flag
    Given a draft shorter than the profile minWords
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there is no low_information_density finding
```
description.to:
**Follow-on under `PPY-54055d`.** Catalog **established** editorial/NLP signals and fuse the ones we can compute into diagnose as independent red flags. Do not invent new NLP methods in this slice.

## Intent

As a publication operator, I want a named list of signals other people already use, each able to raise a steer-able finding, so diagnose is a fusion of known techniques rather than a homemade detector.

## Catalog (v1)

Each row is a known technique. **Ship** = already in diagnose or add now. **Later** = known but not this PR.

| Signal | Established as | Finding (if flagged) | v1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Banned hedges / intensifiers | House style lists; Chatticus `rules.yml` | `vague_claim` | ship (have) |
| Empty lead-ins | Common slop/style lists | `empty_leadin` | ship (have) |
| List-shaped prose | Common LLM-slop pattern lists | `list_shaped_prose` | ship (have) |
| Unsupported certainty | Journalism / hedge-vs-boost (Hyland) | `unsupported_certainty` | ship (have) |
| Repeated n-grams | Self-repetition / ROUGE-style n-gram overlap | `redundancy` | ship (have, 4-gram) |
| Passive voice | Classic style checkers | `voice_mismatch` | ship (have, partial) |
| Numeric claim without attribution | Newsroom attribution norms | `missing_attribution` | ship (have) |
| Contrast-stack cap | House style (Chatticus) | `voice_mismatch` | ship (have, optional) |
| **Lexical density** | Ure (1971); Halliday — content words / total words | `low_lexical_density` | **add** |
| **gzip ratio** | Compression as Kolmogorov-complexity proxy | `high_compressibility` | **add** |
| Type-token ratio / MTLD | McCarthy; McCarthy & Jarvis — lexical diversity | `low_lexical_diversity` | later |
| Flesch–Kincaid / readability | Flesch (1948) | `readability` | later |
| Propositional idea density | CPIDR; Nun Study | (idea density) | later |
| Sentence-embedding paraphrase clusters | STS / summarization duplicates | `concept_restatement` | **not v1** (not a density measure) |

Fusion: each enabled signal may emit its own finding. No single weighted “quality score.” Thresholds live on the style profile. Detector-score keys stay forbidden.

## Done when

- A checked-in catalog (YAML next to the Anth.us profile or `publications/anthus/editorial-signals.yml`) lists signal id, literature/practice name, finding kind, and whether diagnose implements it.
- Diagnose still runs existing signals.
- v1 **adds** lexical density and gzip ratio as independent findings (and a `density` summary with `wordCount`, `sentenceCount`, `lexicalDensity`, `gzipRatio` — no `embedder`).
- Profile `checks.informationDensity` (or per-signal checks) can disable the new pair. Short drafts below `minWords` do not get document-level density findings.
- Behave covers: summary present; long padded fluff flags; Anth.us reference excerpt does not; short draft skips; JSON has no embedder field.
- No sentence embeddings, no TF-IDF clustering, no concept-count invention.

## Gherkin

```gherkin
Feature: Fuse established density signals into diagnose
  As a publication operator
  I want lexical density and compression as named red flags
  So diagnose uses known techniques before any custom NLP

  Scenario: Catalog names the v1 signals
    Given the editorial signals catalog
    Then it lists lexical density and gzip ratio as implemented
    And it does not list sentence embeddings as a v1 implemented signal

  Scenario: Density summary is present
    Given a loadable style profile with information density enabled
    And a draft of several sentences
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then the JSON includes density with wordCount, sentenceCount, lexicalDensity, and gzipRatio
    And the JSON does not include an embedder field

  Scenario: Long low-content fluff is flagged
    Given a draft longer than the profile minWords that is padded with function words and repeats
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there is a low_lexical_density or high_compressibility finding

  Scenario: House-voice excerpt is not flagged as fluff
    Given a must-pass excerpt from an Anth.us reference sample longer than minWords
    And the Anth.us style profile
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there is no low_lexical_density finding
    And there is no high_compressibility finding

  Scenario: Short drafts skip the document-level density flags
    Given a draft shorter than the profile minWords
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there is no low_lexical_density finding
    And there is no high_compressibility finding
```
